hypotheses.statement: The dominant event-142 difference is caused by positional/ordered dithering or by MSAA differences confined to coverage edges.
evidence: Confirmed difference: the sealed final framebuffer differs on 1,160,291 / 1,930,176 pixels (60.11%), max_channel_error 70, alpha_different_pixels 0; the later event-284 fb:0 copy source remains divergent at 1,234,383 / 1,930,176, max 104.
replay/replay.json checkpoint event 142 target 0: 871,620 / 1,930,176 mismatched pixels, max_channel_error 103, alpha_different_pixels 0, mean_abs_error [0.2769, 0.2291, 0.2281, 0.0].
Recomputed |GL-Metal| histogram at event 142: 821,783 pixels at max channel error 1, 49,206 at 2, 631 at >=3, 162 at >=8; 94.28% of all differing pixels are exactly 1 LSB.

Signed Metal-GL 1-LSB counts are strongly asymmetric (B: 440,090 darker vs 7,385 lighter; G: 414,651 vs 13,412; R: 414,064 vs 12,512) and their fraction has no dependence on (x mod 2/4/8, y mod 2/4/8) (per-cell standard deviation <= 0.0023).

Ordered dithering would be position/pattern dependent and bounded by 1 LSB; MSAA differences confined to coverage edges would concentrate there. The 1-LSB bulk is instead interior and unstructured (only 17.3% of 1-LSB pixels sit on a reference gradient >=16 versus 13.1% of the frame under the pilot's gradient metric), while the 162 >=8-LSB pixels are 71.6% edge-located. This excludes those signatures as the dominant cause; it does not exclude a dithering implementation that is not position-ordered, or an MSAA resolve difference that is not edge-confined, because no A/B toggle exists. agent-diagnosis.json lists gl_dither and multisample as unsupported but does not attribute the difference to them.

test.method: Computed per-channel signed error histograms, 1-LSB sign dependence on pixel position modulo 2/4/8, and local-gradient/edge correlation directly from the sealed event-142 GL reference (capture/blobs/default-checkpoint-d77fa555…bin) and Metal checkpoint (replay/intermediate-event142-tex0.bgra).
test.result: Positional/ordered dithering and coverage-edge-confined MSAA are excluded as the dominant cause by the measured pattern. A broad 'dithering or MSAA explains it' claim is not refuted and is not made; no A/B attribution to either state exists.

hypotheses.statement: The event-142 divergence was produced by the immediately preceding program-331 water draws (events 134-141; candidate producer event 141).
evidence: capture/frame-events.jsonl: events 20-141 are 122 consecutive program-331 _GfxDrawIndexed draws (events 14-19 are program 301); event 141 and event 142 share program 331, the same 10 sampler/texture bindings and the same render state, so event 141 is only the last same-resource producer, not a measured source.

replay/replay-provenance.jsonl: all 2,739 bindings, including the 10 bindings at each of events 134-142, have expected_texture == selected_texture and fault_missing_engine_unit == -1; no texture substitution, sampler shift or first-sample-before-write is recorded.

shaders/c08cc785…frag.metal versus the captured c08cc785…frag.glsl: sampler order/mapping, uniform block layout, clip/discard, refract/pow/normalize, snow/fog/shadow helper semantics and constants (SHADOW_WEIGHT_RIVER=0.4, SNOW_WATER_COLOR=(0.5,0.7,0.7)) are preserved; no semantic translation defect was found in the audited paths.

The difference is not confined to water: on reference-land patches (e.g. central France rgb≈[139,112,95]) 95.2% of pixels differ with mean error 0.98, and 122 water draws cannot paint land interiors; therefore a divergence is already present from the program-301 pass (events 14-19) or earlier.

capture/frame-events.jsonl event 7 is a full color+depth+stencil clear of framebuffer 0. It is an operational search boundary, not a matching checkpoint: there is no fb:0 observation at event 7, and no fb:0 checkpoint exists between it and event 142 (agent-diagnosis.json first_divergence.unresolved_interval.start_event is null). The interval therefore remains unbounded with a post-clear search start of 7; event 7 is not a proven matching lower bound.

test.method: Audited events 134-142 draw state, texture/sampler bindings, the program-331 GLSL-to-MSL translation and the replay provenance; measured the event-142 difference separately over reference land and sea regions.
test.result: The candidate producer can be neither confirmed nor excluded. The water-only version is contradicted by the land-region differences, but no earlier fb:0 observation exists to place the first producer.

hypotheses.statement: The dominant 1-LSB component of the event-142 difference is consistent with numerical/quantization variation in the fixed-function/texture pipeline rather than a texture-binding or shader-content mismatch.
evidence: Of 871,620 differing event-142 pixels, 821,783 (94.28%) have a 1-LSB maximum channel error, alpha is identical everywhere (alpha_different_pixels 0), and the spatial sign is asymmetric and unstructured (see H1).

The same 1-LSB signature exists earlier in the identical sealed frame on a different resource: the tex:433 checkpoint (event 270; producer events 0-6 per replay/checkpoint-request.json) differs on 574,288 RGB pixels after the required RGB8/BGRA8 channel normalization (569,880 at 1 LSB, 4,408 at 2, only 3 at >=8; max 109; mean RGB error 0.125). That checkpoint is classified diagnostic by the case comparator and is therefore supplementary only, not an authoritative first-divergence observation.

Captured texture levels are uploaded as decompressed RGBA8 (benchmark/eu4_gfx_frame_replay.mm build_texture reads levels[*].pixel_format), so DXT5/DXT3 decode cannot be a difference source; combined with the 2,739/2,739 expected-binding provenance, no binding or upload defect is supported.

The residual 5.7% of differing pixels (>=2 LSB, 631 at >=3) is edge-localized and is not explained by this component. The numerical-variation reading is a hypothesis consistent with the observations; it does not establish a pipeline mechanism and does not isolate one numeric stage (GL fixed-point filtering/quantization, fixed-point blending, or shader arithmetic).

test.method: Error histogram, alpha and spatial/edge characterization, the independent tex:433 producer comparison, and a provenance plus texture-upload/shader audit.
test.result: Consistent with a numerical-variation hypothesis for the dominant 1-LSB component. It does not establish a pipeline mechanism or a root cause, and does not explain the edge-localized residual.

evidence_request.reason: The sealed case contains no fb:0 observation between the event-7 full color+depth+stencil clear and the event-142 pre-draw checkpoint. Event 7 is an operational search boundary, not a matching checkpoint. The only matched checkpoints (events 11 and 13) are all-white pre-draw images of the ping-pong shadow-blur buffers, so they validate neither the post-clear fb:0 nor any drawn map content. The first producer of the confirmed difference therefore cannot be placed between the post-clear program-301 map pass (events 14-19) and the 122 program-331 water draws (events 20-141); the land-region differences in H2 show the water pass alone cannot explain it.
evidence_request.cross_frame_caveat: A new capture has a new session_id, capture_frame_id and event_stream_sha256. Its checkpoints cannot be combined with event 142 of sealed frame 1 even if the scene parameters match, and no cross-capture causal interval may be formed. The new frame must independently reproduce the divergence (its own final-frame comparison) and must be analyzed entirely within its own seal.

checkpoints.why: Pre-draw observation of the default framebuffer at the first content draw after the event-7 full color+depth+stencil clear. It decides whether the post-clear fb:0 already diverges before the program-301 map pass, which is the earliest possible producer compatible with the event-142 observation.

Pre-draw observation at the first program-331 water draw. Together with event 14 it separates the program-301 pass (events 14-19) from the 122-draw water pass (20-141) that contains the candidate producer event 141.
Midpoint bisection inside the water pass and the checkpoint recommended by agent-diagnosis.json first_divergence.next_checkpoint; needed only if the event-14 and event-20 observations both match.

evidence_request.evaluation_scope: Each requested checkpoint is compared only with the GL reference captured in the same new sealed frame, within that frame's own seal. No checkpoint from one capture bounds another, and the new frame must reproduce the divergence in its own final-frame comparison.

remaining_uncertainty: The lower bound of the causal interval is unobserved: event 7 is a full clear used only as an operational search boundary, not a matching checkpoint, and no fb:0 observation exists between it and event 142. Event 141 is therefore not established as the producer; the interval remains unbounded with a post-clear search start of 7.

The edge-localized residual (631 pixels at >=3 LSB, 162 at >=8, max 103) is not explained by the 1-LSB mechanism; derivative/LOD selection, coverage or an edge-specific translation defect remain candidates, but no experiment isolates one.

The sampler cache key in benchmark/eu4_gfx_frame_replay.mm omits lodMinClamp, lodMaxClamp, wrap_r, compare mode/function and anisotropy. On the event-142 path the only collision is tex:385 (8 levels, max_lod 7) reusing the tex:374/371 sampler (max_lod 10); that is equivalent because tex:385 has only 8 levels, but the key remains incomplete for other frames.

gl_dither and multisample are still captured-but-unimplemented and remain unattributed by an A/B toggle; this pilot excludes only positional/ordered dithering and coverage-edge-confined MSAA signatures as the dominant cause, not the states themselves.

The tex:433 checkpoint is classified diagnostic (RGB8 internal format versus the BGRA8 render-target emulation); its post-normalization statistics are supplementary only, are not an authoritative first-divergence observation, and are not used to bound the interval.

The Metal replay records target/transfer/provenance and per-draw bindings, but not the applied per-draw blend/depth/stencil pipeline state, so a state-level mismatch cannot be excluded from the replay artifact alone.
next_experiment: Capture one new sealed frame of the identical selection with a pre-event fb:0 checkpoint at event 14, replay it through the existing metal replay path, and compare it against its own GL reference within its own capture identity; if event 14 matches, repeat with event 20 to separate the program-301 pass from the program-331 water pass, then event 71 for midpoint bisection.
